architecture_security_shape.summary: Single-process Flask app where route handlers, helper functions, database bootstrap, keys and security-sensitive consumers share one module/global process context.
architecture_security_shape.dominant_security_characteristic: Unauthenticated HTTP entry points transfer client-controlled values directly into high-authority consumers such as eval, os.popen, pickle.loads, lxml parsing, Jinja rendering, AES decrypt/unpad, JWT verification and SQL cursor execution.

security_critical_modules_components.security_role: Receives all external HTTP input and dispatches to local consumers.
/lookup builds a command and calls popen through rp().
/cookie deserializes client cookie data with pickle.
/sayhi constructs a template from form input and renders it.
Startup creates/loads database state; /listservices executes SQL using global cursor.
/user/login, /user and /user/jwks issue, verify and expose JWT trust material.
/config exposes AES-CBC decrypt/unpad behavior and looks up CONFIG.
/xml parses request XML with DTD loading and network-enabled options.
CLI/environment controls address, database connection and key-file loading.

high_value_assets_sensitive_data_paths.description: Holds globals, keys, DB cursor and host privileges for all workflows.
Controls authentication cookie validity and admin-state decision.
Contains base64-encoded KEY and ADMIN_SECRET values in memory.
public_stuff is route-exposed; secret_stuff is seeded but not normal-route exposed.
Reachability depends on process and parser/command behavior.
CLI can pass DB username/password/host/port; app may create/use breakdb.

privileged_high_impact_business_operatio.description: /user displays admin success when verified JWT claims contain sub == admin.
/user/login accepts guest:guest, creates RS256 token and sets authentication cookie.
Startup creates databases/tables and inserts seed data; /listservices reads through global cursor.
Routes cross from web input to interpreter, OS, deserializer, template engine, parser and decryptor boundaries.

authentication_authorization_surfaces.description: Authentication is isolated to the /user flow; no global auth middleware protects other sensitive routes.
authentication cookie controls /user; algorithm dispatch uses token header; authorization checks sub against ADMIN_USER.
Key material is loaded from PRIVATE_KEY_FILE/PUBLIC_KEY_FILE when present or generated into temp files otherwise.

security_controls_relevant.baseline_note: Exposure changes if --address is set differently.
Present in RS256 and manual HS256/None verification paths.
Admin state depends on sub == admin.
Applies after XML parsing, not before parser resource handling.

security_controls_relevant.control: Linked config keys limited to app_ prefix
security_controls_relevant.baseline_note: Decrypted query selectors are checked against all CONFIG keys.
Exceptions are returned as response text.
Backend behavior differs across supported engines.

limited_visibility_unresolved_behavior: No SECURITY.md, production deployment manifest, WSGI server config, CI workflow or test suite was identified in the prior intelligence pass.
Actual exposure of routes depends on runtime --address and host/network configuration.
External database behavior depends on selected backend, driver behavior, DB user privileges and server configuration.
Process-level impact depends on host permissions, environment, installed commands and runtime context.
XML external resource behavior depends on lxml/libxml2 behavior and deployment filesystem/network policy.
JWT exploitability details depend on runtime PyJWT behavior, token construction and clock validation; pre-scan does not validate exploitability.

important_dependencies.dependency: Process authority is shared across route handlers, config, keys and DB cursor.
JWT trust depends on key initialization and algorithm dispatch.
Database runtime depends on __main__ startup creating cursor and query_build.
Config crypto depends on process-lifetime KEY.

threat_convergence.area: Process authority via direct execution consumers
threat_convergence.prioritization_reason: Multiple independent entry points may converge on keys, config, DB cursor and host permissions.
/listservices directly reaches SQL; process-level paths may also reach cursor or DB modules.
JWT authorization can be affected directly by token verification behavior or indirectly by process/config/key exposure.
OS command execution and XML parser behavior both cross toward host or network resources; process-level paths may do the same.
JWT and config flows both make security decisions based on attacker-influenced encoded or cryptographic material.

standard_scan.target_module_component_api_flow: Whole repository, with primary attention to main.py route handlers, helper functions and startup path.
standard_scan.relevant_security_concern_or_threat_cont: Baseline scan should cover all externally reachable route-to-sensitive-consumer flows and shared-process consequences.
standard_scan.related_asset_or_business_function: Flask process authority, authentication/admin state, database contents, config secrets and host/file/network resources.
standard_scan.reason_scan_focus_is_valuable: The repo is small and monolithic; a whole-repo pass can correlate all route flows, globals and startup-dependent resources without scope fragmentation.

deep_scan.relevant_security_concern_or_threat_cont: Multiple distinct trust-boundary failures converge on process authority, database authority, key material and host resources.
deep_scan.related_asset_or_business_function: Process authority, JWT keys/admin authorization, CONFIG hidden entries, DB tables and local/network resources.
deep_scan.related_threat_scenario_or_attack_path: Process-authority convergence T1-T4; database linkage T5; authentication/key-material linkage T6-T7; parser/resource linkage T8.
deep_scan.reason_scan_focus_is_valuable: Deep review should reduce variance across several independent high-impact paths and inspect cross-threat relationships rather than only isolated line-level patterns.

module_scan.target_module_component_api_flow: main.py logical modules: JWT/auth helpers and /user*; DB bootstrap and /listservices; config crypto and /config; parser/evaluation/execution routes.
module_scan.relevant_security_concern_or_threat_cont: Although physically one file, the code has distinct security modules with separate trust boundaries and shared globals.
module_scan.related_asset_or_business_function: Authentication/admin state, database contents, hidden config values and process/OS/template/parser authority.
module_scan.related_threat_scenario_or_attack_path: JWT module T6; DB module T5; config crypto T7; parser/execution routes T1-T4 and T8.
module_scan.reason_scan_focus_is_valuable: Module-oriented review can preserve logical boundaries inside the monolith and inspect each module's caller/callee relationships and shared-state dependencies.

exploitable_scan.target_module_component_api_flow: Reachability-oriented validation candidates for /evaluate, /lookup, /cookie, /sayhi, /listservices, /config, /xml and /user*, without expanding beyond authorized app behavior.
exploitable_scan.relevant_security_concern_or_threat_cont: Determine which source-backed threat paths are practically reachable under actual runtime semantics and default or documented configurations.
exploitable_scan.related_asset_or_business_function: Process authority, host resources, DB contents, hidden config and authentication/admin state.
exploitable_scan.related_threat_scenario_or_attack_path: T1-T8, with emphasis on preconditions and controls recorded in Scan Report-2.
exploitable_scan.reason_scan_focus_is_valuable: The pre-scan baseline identifies many intentional threat paths; an exploitable scan should distinguish source-backed theoretical reachability from practically demonstrable behavior without assigning final severity at this stage.
